result.topic_en: A lemma and Problem I with its solution: every divisor D of p^2+nq^2 (with p, q coprime) can be written as frr ± gqr + hqq with 4fh − gg = 4n, followed by a corollary and a scholion on how little this general form helps in practice.
result.transcription:
Lemma.
§. 2. Si $p$ et $q$ fuerint numeri inter se primi, tum omnes plane numeri in hac forma generali $\alpha p \pm \beta q$ comprehendi possint, idque infinitis modis. Huius lemmatis demonstratio per se facilis passim inuenitur.

Problema I.
§. 3. Si p et q sint numeri inter se primi, n vero denotet numerum quemcunque datum, siue positiuum siue negatiuum, inuenire omnes diuisores huius formulae: $pp+nqq$.

Solutio.
Denotet D diuisorem quemcunque numeri in hac forma $pp+nqq$ contenti, sitque $d$ quotus ex hac diuisione ortus, ita vt sit $Dd=pp+nqq$. Hic iam statim euidens est, numerum $d$ ad $q$ fore primum; si enim $q$ haberet diuisorem communem, eundem quoque $p$ habere deberet, contra hypothesin, quamobrem numerus $p$ per $d$ et $q$ ita exprimi poterit, vt sit $p=\alpha d \pm \beta q$, quo valore substituto fiet
$Dd=\alpha\alpha dd \pm 2\alpha\beta dq + (\beta\beta+n)qq$
ideoque diuisor
$D=\alpha\alpha d \pm 2\alpha\beta q + (\frac{\beta\beta+n}{d})qq$,
vbi ergo $\frac{\beta\beta+n}{d}$ erit numerus integer, qui sit $=h$, ita vt habeatur
$D=\alpha\alpha d \pm 2\alpha\beta q + hqq$,
pro qua forma scribamus
$D=frr \pm gqr + hqq$,
ita vt sit $f=d$, $r=\alpha$, $g=2\beta$ et ob $h=\frac{\beta\beta+n}{f}$ erit $fh=\beta\beta+n$; hincque fiet $4fh-gg=4n$. Hinc igitur patet, omnes diuisores formae $pp+nqq$ semper contineri in hac forma:
$D=frr \pm gqr + hqq$,
dummodo fuerit $4fh-gg=4n$. Ac vicissim, si fuerit
$D=frr \pm gqr + hqq$, erit
$4df=4ffrr \pm 4fgqr + 4fhqq$;
ideoque ob $4fh=4n+gg$, erit
$4Df=(2fr \pm gq)^2+4nqq$,
quae forma a proposita non discrepat, si modo diuidatur per 4.

Corollarium 1.
§. 4. In genere igitur omnes diuisores formulae propositae $pp+nqq$ comprehendere licebit in ista formula latissime patente: $frr+grs+hss$, dummodo fuerit $4fh-gg=4n$, siue $fh-\frac{1}{4}gg=n$; vnde patet, innumeras huiusmodi formulas exhiberi posse, quoniam numerum $g$ pro lubitu accipere licet. Ex eo autem numeros $f$ et $h$ ita definiri oportet, vt fiat $4fh=4n+gg$.

Scholion.
§. 5. Quoniam autem innumerabiles huiusmodi formulas: $frr+grs+hss$, exhibere licet, in quibus sit $4fh-gg=4n$, parum hinc lucri ad nostrum institutum afferri videtur. Proposito enim quocunque numero D, ad diiudicandum, vtrum esse possit diuisor formae $pp+nqq$, omnes illae innumerabiles formulae considerari deberent,
num
M m 3

items.quote: Si $p$ et $q$ fuerint numeri inter se primi, tum omnes plane numeri in hac forma generali $\alpha p \pm \beta q$ comprehendi possint, idque infinitis modis.
items.english: If p and q are coprime, then absolutely all numbers can be contained in the general form αp ± βq, and in infinitely many ways.

items.quote: Si p et q sint numeri inter se primi, n vero denotet numerum quemcunque datum, siue positiuum siue negatiuum, inuenire omnes diuisores huius formulae: $pp+nqq$.
items.english: If p and q are coprime and n denotes any given number, positive or negative, find all divisors of the formula pp+nqq.

items.quote: In genere igitur omnes diuisores formulae propositae $pp+nqq$ comprehendere licebit in ista formula latissime patente: $frr+grs+hss$, dummodo fuerit $4fh-gg=4n$
items.english: In general, therefore, all divisors of the proposed formula pp+nqq can be contained in this very broad formula frr+grs+hss, provided that 4fh−gg=4n.
